facts.statement: The genus Romeosaurus was first described by Palci and colleagues in 2013.
facts.quote: authority: Palci et al., 2013

facts.statement: Romeosaurus fossils date to the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Romeosaurus is an extinct yaguarasaurine mosasaur found in the Lastame lithotype of northern Italy, dating from the lower Turonian to lower Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Romeosaurus is an extinct genus of yaguarasaurine mosasaur known from the early Late Cretaceous "Lastame" lithotype (lower Turonian to lower Santonian) of northern Italy.

facts.statement: The species Romeosaurus sorbinii is known only from a single, very fragmented specimen and remains poorly described.
facts.quote: Of the 2 species, R. sorbinii is known only through very fragmented fossil records of a single specimen and is otherwise poorly described.

facts.statement: The species Romeosaurus fumanensis is known from multiple specimens found across a small area in Italy.
facts.quote: R. fumanensis is known through more specimens found across a small geographic area in Italy.

facts.statement: No recovered specimens of Romeosaurus have well-preserved post-cranial fossils, making it difficult to determine their body anatomy beyond the skull.
facts.quote: Of all specimens recovered, none had well enough preserved post-cranial fossils to make good judgments of their post-cranial anatomy.

facts.statement: As of 2018, only one specimen of R. sorbinii and four specimens of R. fumanensis were known to science.
facts.quote: As of 2018, only 1 specimen of R. sorbinii and 4 specimens of R. fumanensis were known.

facts.statement: The genus name Romeosaurus honors the character Romeo from Shakespeare's play, referencing the proximity of the fossil sites to Verona.
facts.quote: The genus is named after the character Romeo in William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, due to the proximity of the locations of the fossils to Verona, where the play is set.

facts.statement: The species R. sorbinii is named after paleontologist Lorenzo Sorbini, while R. fumanensis is named after the town of Fumane.
facts.quote: R. sorbinii is named after Lorenzo Sorbini, an Italian paleontologist, whilst R. fumanensis is named after Fumane, a comune in the Province of Verona.

facts.statement: Romeosaurus is classified within the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Yaguarasaurinae

facts.statement: Romeosaurus lived in northern Italy during the early Late Cretaceous, specifically between the early Turonian and early Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Romeosaurus es un género extinto de mosasáurido yaguasaurino que vivió a principios del Cretácico Superior en el litotipo "Lastame" (entre principios del Turoniense a principios del Santoniense) en el norte de Italia.

facts.statement: Romeosaurus was a medium-sized mosasaur, comparable to Clidastes, and likely did not exceed 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Romeosaurus era un mosasáurido de dimensiones medianas, comparables a las de Clidastes, y no debía de superar los 3 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Like other mosasaurs, Romeosaurus had a fusiform body with limbs adapted for swimming.
facts.quote: Como todos los mosasáuridos, Romeosaurus tenía un cuerpo fusiforme y con sus cuatro extremidades adaptadas a la natación.

facts.statement: The type species, R. fumanensis, is known from four incomplete specimens that were sufficient to reconstruct its appearance.
facts.quote: La especie tipo es Romeosaurus fumanensis, conocida de cuatro ejemplares incompletos, pero suficientes para reconstruir su aspecto.

facts.statement: R. fumanensis possessed a relatively thin skull with about 15 strongly recurved teeth on each side of the jaws.
facts.quote: R. fumanensis poseía un cráneo relativamente delgado, con unos 15 dientes muy recurvados presentes de cada lado de los maxilares.

facts.statement: The crowns of the upper jaw teeth of R. fumanensis were smooth, lacking any ornamentation on the enamel.
facts.quote: La corona dental de los dientes maxilares eran lisas, sin presentar algún tipo de ornamentación en su esmalte.

facts.statement: R. sorbinii is known from a single specimen and differs from R. fumanensis by having a different frontal bone shape, fewer upper jaw teeth (13), and ornamented tooth enamel.
facts.quote: La especie R. sorbinii es conocida por un único espécimen, y se diferencia de la anterior por la forma diferente del hueso frontal, por el número menor de dientes en el maxilar (13) y por la presencia de ornamentación en el esmalte dental.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis indicates Romeosaurus is a close relative of the North American Russellosaurus and the South American Yaguarasaurus, forming the primitive subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético efectuado por sus descriptores (Palci et al., 2013) indica que Romeosaurus es considerado como un pariente cercano de Russellosaurus, un mosasauroide norteamericano; asimismo está relacionado con un género suramericano, Yaguarasaurus, representando estos una subfamilia de mosasáuridos primitivos que fue denominada como Yaguarasaurinae

facts.statement: Romeosaurus was distinguished from Russellosaurus, Tethysaurus, and Pannoniasaurus by the presence of a pre-dental rostrum in the jaw.
facts.quote: Romeosaurus poseía una característica que lo diferenciaba de Russellosaurus, Tethysaurus y Pannoniasaurus: la presencia de un rostro predental en la mandíbula.

facts.statement: Research by Palci et al. supports the hypothesis that the evolution of limbs into fin-like structures occurred twice independently within mosasaurs.
facts.quote: El estudio de Palci et al. también ha reforzado la hipótesis según la cual, dentro del grupo de los mosasáuridos, la evolución de las patas hacia estructuras similares a las aletas ocurrió dos veces

facts.statement: Romeosaurus fossils were recovered from the Scaglia Rossa Veneta formation, specifically the Lastame lithozone, which was an open sea environment during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Romeosaurus se han recuperado en la formación geológica de Scaglia Rossa Veneta, y más precisamente en la litozona conocida como "Lastame", que se supone que fue una zona de mar abierto durante el Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: The open marine environment of the Lastame lithozone is supported by finds of marine vertebrates like Cretoxyrhina and Ptychodus, as well as ammonites and planktonic foraminifera.
facts.quote: Esto se ha comprobado con los hallazgos de numerosos vertebrados marinos (como los tiburones Cretoxyrhina y Ptychodus, y la tortuga Protosphargis), así como de ammonites y de foraminíferos planctónicos.

facts.statement: The parent group of Romeosaurus is Yaguarasaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Yaguarasaurinae

facts.statement: Romeosaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Romeosaurus lived from the Turonian to the Santonian stages, approximately 93.9 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Santonian (93.9 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Romeosaurus was first described in 2013 based on fossils found in caves between Monte Loffa and the town of Fumane in the Monti Lessini.
rejected.quote: Romeosaurus fue descrito por primera vez en 2013, basándose en los restos fósiles encontrados en algunas cuevas entre el Monte Loffa y el pueblo de Fumane, en los Monti Lessini.
